name: idempotent-request
documentation: Answers a repeated request with the stored answer: the request id (x-ms-client-request-id) is the key in the platform's distributed cache.

input.title: PaymentRequest
input.documentation: Starts idempotent-request with a PaymentRequest. x-ms-client-request-id and Accept-Language are fields of the input: in the designer they go into the input JSON, a published plugin fills them from the request headers.

steps.name: read the request id
steps.note: x-ms-client-request-id names the request: a retry after a lost response carries the same id. Without it: 400. The key starts with the Flow's name, because every Flow on the installation shares the cache.

steps.name: look for the stored answer
steps.note: Shared by every server of the installation: a retry finds the answer wherever the first call ran. While the work runs the key holds 'pending': a parallel retry gets 409. No cache: 503. The stored answer is read back here, so a damaged entry takes the error branch.

steps.name: answered before?
steps.note: yes: the stored answer goes back unchanged, the work is not done again.

steps.name: answer as before
accept the payment
store the answer
steps.note: Kept for cacheSeconds from the configuration Flow. A failure to store is logged and the answer still goes back; the retry then does the work again.

Ev_End.name: answered and stored
Ev_End.title: ADDED
Ev_End.documentation: Success, HTTP 201: the work is done and the answer stored; cacheStatus Added.

Ev_Replayed.name: answered from the cache
Ev_Replayed.title: IS_COMPLETED
Ev_Replayed.documentation: Success, HTTP 201: a repeated request id; the stored answer, cacheStatus IsCompleted.

failure.name: request refused
failure.title: NO_REQUEST_ID
failure.documentation: Refusal: HTTP 400 without x-ms-client-request-id, 409 while the same request is in progress, 503 when the cache is not available; message in the caller's language.
